'''Samuel Charles Conway'''<ref group="‡">{{cite web|url=http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=R0VPvet9biA#t=7204 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150522185050/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=R0VPvet9biA |archive-date=May 22, 2015 |url-status=dead|title=Uncle Kage's Winestream @ FURSTRE.AM|author=Conway, Samuel C.| website=[[YouTube]] |date=December 8, 2013|access-date=December 27, 2013}}</ref> (born June 4, 1965) is an American researcher in the [[pharmaceutical]], [[biomedical]] and [[agrochemical]] fields of [[organic chemistry]]. He holds a [[Ph.D.]] in [[chemistry]] from [[Dartmouth College]]. Aside from his scientific career, Conway is known for his activities in the [[furry fandom]], having served since 1999 as [[chairman]] and chief organizer of [[Anthrocon]], one of the largest [[furry convention]]s in the world.<ref>{{cite news|title=Anthrocons convention turns city into 'real zoo'|url=http://www.post-gazette.com/pg/07188/799987-51.stm|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070709152703/http://www.post-gazette.com/pg/07188/799987-51.stm|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 9, 2007|author=Carpenter, Mackenzie|newspaper=[[Pittsburgh Post-Gazette]]|date=July 7, 2007|access-date=April 10, 2009}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Anthrocon Is Back, And Pittsburgh's Feeling Furry Again|url=http://www.thepittsburghchannel.com/news/16715461/detail.html|publisher=[[WTAE-TV]]|date=June 28, 2008|access-date=April 10, 2009|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080630222207/http://www.thepittsburghchannel.com/news/16715461/detail.html|archive-date=June 30, 2008}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Anthrocon 2007 draws thousands to Pittsburgh for furry weekend|url=http://en.wikinews.org/wiki/Anthrocon_2007_draws_thousands_to_Pittsburgh_for_furry_weekend|publisher=[[Wikinews]]|date=July 17, 2007|access-date=April 10, 2009}}</ref> He is a published author, and has acted as a volunteer emergency coordinator, entertainer, and auctioneer.

== Academic and scientific activities ==

A graduate of [[Ursinus College]], [[Pennsylvania]] in 1986, Conway subsequently studied at the Burke Chemical Laboratories of Dartmouth College, [[New Hampshire]], where he obtained his Ph.D. in 1991.<ref name="KageTheMan" group="‡"/><ref name="MadSci">{{cite web|url=http://www.madsci.org/hofbios/conway_s.html|title=Mad Scientist Network Hall of Fame – Samual C. Conway|access-date=August 27, 2006}}</ref><ref group="‡">{{cite web|url=http://unclekage.livejournal.com/profile?mode=full|title=unclekage – User Info|author=Conway, Samuel C.|access-date=August 27, 2006}}</ref> His [[doctoral thesis|thesis]] concerned the attempted generation of ''indolyne'' (an [[aromatic compound]] related to [[indole]]).<ref name="Gribble"/><ref name="Indolyne">{{cite journal|title=Approaches to the Generation of 2,3-Indolyne|author1=Conway, S.C. |author2=Gribble, G.W. |journal=[[Heterocycles (journal)|Heterocycles]] |pages=2095–2108|doi=10.3987/COM-92-6105|year=1992|volume=34|issue=11|doi-access=free}}</ref>

After college, Conway took a [[postdoctoral research|postdoctoral appointment]] in [[Chicago]], later working as a contractor for the [[Food and Drug Administration]], a researcher for Bionetics, a [[medicinal chemistry|medicinal chemist]] for Avid Therapeutics (March 1995 – August 1997) and researcher for Message Pharmaceuticals (August 1997 – April 1999).<ref name="LinkedIn">{{cite web|title=Samuel Conway|url=http://www.linkedin.com/pub/3/798/857|publisher=[[LinkedIn]]|access-date=April 3, 2009}}</ref> He spent two years in organ distribution at the [[National Disease Research Interchange]], and was subsequently employed by crop protection company Cerexagri<!--merged with United Phosphorus--> as a regulatory chemist from May 2001 to June 2007, when he became a principal chemist for [[West Pharmaceutical Services]].<ref name="KageTheMan" group="‡"/><ref name="LinkedIn" /> As of July 2013, he was working for a group near [[Raleigh, North Carolina]].<ref name="NewJob" group="‡">{{cite web|url=http://unclekage.livejournal.com/145548.html|title=A new job, a new home, a new life|author=Conway, Samuel C.|date=November 4, 2013|access-date=November 5, 2013}}</ref>

Conway has authored eleven [[academic publishing#Scholarly paper|professional publications]] and two<!--Not three, per email from subject --GreenReaper --> patents.<ref name="KageTheMan" group="‡"/> One patent covers compounds intended to treat [[hepatitis B]] in synergy with [[lamivudine]];<ref>Perni, Robert B.; Conway, Samuel C. (August 6, 1998) WO patent 98/33501, ''[https://patentscope.wipo.int/search/en/detail.jsf?docId=WO1998033501 "2-Benzoylamino-3-phenylpropenamide derivatives and methods of using the same"]'', filed 1998-01-29, U.S. pri date 1997-01-3, Avid Therapeutics. WIPO. Patentscope.</ref><ref name="Inhibition">{{cite journal|title=Inhibition of Human Hepatitis B Virus Replication by AT-61, a Phenylpropenamide Derivative, Alone and in Combination with (−)β-l-2′,3′-Dideoxy-3′-Thiacytidine|author1=King, Robert W. |author2=Ladner, Stephanie K. |author3=Miller, Thomas J. |author4=Zaifert, Katie |author5=Perni, Robert B. |author6=Conway, Samuel C. |author7=Otto, Michael J. |journal=[[Antimicrobial Agents and Chemotherapy]] |date=June 22, 1998|pmc=106020|volume=42|issue=12|pmid=9835512|pages=3179–3186 |doi=10.1128/AAC.42.12.3179 }}</ref> another relates to recyclable packaging material.<ref>Barenberg, Sumner A. et al. == Fandom activities ==
Conway was introduced to the [[furry fandom]] at [[47th World Science Fiction Convention|Noreascon 3]] (the 1989 [[Worldcon]]),<ref>{{cite web|title=The Jim Groat Interview |url=http://furry101.com/?p=183 |publisher=Furry 101 |date=March 27, 2009 |access-date=March 27, 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100217142403/http://furry101.com/?p=183 |archive-date=February 17, 2010 }}</ref> and has been involved in [[fandom|fan activities]] from the early 1990s to the present day.

=== Convention chairman ===
[[Image:Anthrocon 2007 Kage Bennie Rigel KP Giza closing ceremonies.jpg|right|thumb|200px| Conway with Anthrocon staff, 2007]]

Conway became the chairman of Anthrocon in 1999, after his invitation as a guest of honor in 1998.<ref name="KageStoryteller" group="‡">{{cite web|url=http://www.unclekage.com/storyteller.html|title=Uncle Kage – The Storyteller|author=Conway, Samuel C.|access-date=August 27, 2006}}</ref> Under his leadership, Anthrocon was incorporated and moved to [[Philadelphia]]. The convention's attendance grew from 842 to 2,489 over the period from 1999 to 2006, necessitating a further move to [[Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania|Pittsburgh]]; 3,390 attended in 2008.<ref>{{cite web|title=About Anthrocon|url=http://www.anthrocon.org/history|publisher=[[Anthrocon]]|access-date=April 10, 2009}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=2008 Registration Totals|url=http://www.anthrocon.org/history-registration-2008|publisher=[[Anthrocon]]|date=August 3, 2008|access-date=April 3, 2009|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090221074324/http://www.anthrocon.org/history-registration-2008|archive-date=February 21, 2009}}</ref> Conway is the public face of Anthrocon, responsible for [[public relations]], negotiating hotel contracts, managing finances, [[Damage control (news)#Spin|damage control]] and other activities before, during and after the convention. He also talks to fans about presenting furry fandom to the public.<ref group="‡">{{cite web|author=Conway, Samuel C.|title=Comment to ''new media article from the seattle weekly''|url=http://www.anthrocon.org/node/1966#comment-14095|date=January 23, 2008|access-date=April 3, 2009|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081008032039/http://www.anthrocon.org/node/1966#comment-14095|archive-date=October 8, 2008}}</ref><ref><!-- PDF marked as obsolete because it's for 2008 -->{{cite web|title=Midwest FurFest 2008 programming panel descriptions (p4, Furry and the Media) |url=http://www.furfest.org/2008/PDF/ProgDesc2008.pdf |publisher=[[Midwest Furry Fandom]] |access-date=April 10, 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090106180652/http://www.furfest.org/2008/PDF/ProgDesc2008.pdf |archive-date=January 6, 2009 }}</ref><ref><!-- Linked from http://www.furryweekend.com/schedule -->{{cite web|title=Furry Weekend Atlanta 2008: Event detail – Presenting Furry Fandom to the Public|url=http://fwa.jinglefox.com/event_details.php?ID=206&conYear=2008|publisher=[[Furry Weekend Atlanta]]|access-date=April 10, 2009|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110713105944/http://fwa.jinglefox.com/event_details.php?ID=206&conYear=2008|archive-date=July 13, 2011}}</ref>

==== Media dealings ====
{{Update|section|reason=Coverage of Conway's media activities largely stops in 2006|date=November 2026}}
[[Image:KageTalksToReportersAC2006.jpg|right|thumb|200px|Conway talks to [[KDKA-TV]] reporters outside Anthrocon 2006.]]

Conway dissuades members of the fandom, and Anthrocon membership in particular, from responding to the [[mass media]] and [[news media]], due in part to sensationalist coverage like the 2001 ''[[Vanity Fair (magazine)|Vanity Fair]]'' article in which he was quoted.<ref name="Pleasures">{{citation|author=Gurley, George|title=Pleasures of the Fur|url=http://www.vanityfair.com/culture/features/2001/03/furries200103|publisher=Vanity Fair|date=March 1, 2001|access-date=August 27, 2006}}</ref> In 2003 he said his standard response to the media was: "Anthrocon is a private event held on private property. Its membership is not interested in being the subject of your documentary."<ref group="‡">{{cite newsgroup|title=Tabloid shows, Confurence, and lay off of Darrell already|author=Conway, Samuel C.|date=April 29, 2003|newsgroup=alt.fan.furry.bleachers|message-id=ro1savk9kum9no9s85fg1j883o2lv6r7td@4ax.com|url=https://groups.google.com/forum/#!original/alt.fan.furry.bleachers/n6Gcrv7uyAE/lXBTO0boOe0J}}</ref>

However, Conway relaxed this stance with Anthrocon's move to Pittsburgh in 2006. While no television, magazine or tabloid representatives were present, several newspapers were invited to attend, and did, including the ''[[Pittsburgh Tribune-Review]]'',<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.pittsburghlive.com/x/pittsburghtrib/news/cityregion/s_458482.html|title=It's a furry weekend|author=Kurutz, Daveen Rae|newspaper=Pittsburgh Tribune-Review|date=June 17, 2006|access-date=August 27, 2006|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060702091113/http://www.pittsburghlive.com/x/pittsburghtrib/news/cityregion/s_458482.html|archive-date=July 2, 2006}}</ref> the ''[[Pittsburgh Post-Gazette]]'',<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.post-gazette.com/lifestyle/2006/06/18/All-about-furry-fandom-at-confab/stories/200606180151|title=All about 'furry fandom' at confab|author=Belser, Ann|newspaper=Pittsburgh Post-Gazette|date=June 18, 2006|access-date=August 27, 2006}}</ref> and the ''[[Pittsburgh City Paper]]'', which printed both a preview and an extensive review.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.pghcitypaper.com/news-2/fur-ball-in-the-works-1336602/|title=Fur Ball In the Works|last=Meinzer|first=Melissa|date=February 2, 2006|newspaper=[[Pittsburgh City Paper]]|access-date=February 2, 2006}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.pghcitypaper.com/news-2/animal-passions-1337258/|title=Animal Passions|last=Meinzer|first=Melissa|date=June 29, 2006|newspaper=[[Pittsburgh City Paper]]|access-date=August 27, 2006}}</ref> When local television station [[KDKA-TV]] showed up, Conway gave a short television interview outside the convention hotel.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://kdka.com/topstories/furries.Pittsburgh.convention.2.383477.html |title=Furries Descend On Pittsburgh |publisher=[[KDKA-TV]] |date=June 16, 2006 |access-date=April 6, 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090706205753/http://kdka.com/topstories/furries.Pittsburgh.convention.2.383477.html |archive-date=July 6, 2009 }}</ref> In November 2006 he gave a radio interview to [[Dublin's 98]]FM.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://giza.livejournal.com/363229.html |title=Radio Interview about Furry Fandom on Dublin 98 FM |author=Muth, Douglas |date=November 8, 2006 |access-date=December 4, 2006 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110721173147/http://giza.livejournal.com/363229.html |archive-date=July 21, 2011 }} [http://lists.claws-and-paws.com/files/Dublin_98_FM_Interview_with_Uncle_Kage_November_8th,_2006.mp3 MP3]{{dead link|date=April 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> Anthrocon still retains tight control over media access, not only to the convention grounds but to the membership, and has official policy<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.anthrocon.org/rules-conduct#media|title=Anthrocon Standards of Conduct}}</ref> that forbids unmonitored dealings with unauthorized members of the media.

=== Storyteller ===

Conway styles himself "Furrydom's Storyteller", making annual appearances at Anthrocon in what has come to be known as ''Uncle Kage's Story Hour''. The entertainment typically consists of four or five extended personal [[anecdote]]s. His [[stage name]] resulted from his first storytelling experience at [[ConFurence]] in 1994, and derives from his [[fandom name]] ''Kagemushi Goro'' (''Shadow Bug Goro''), a reference to ''[[Kagemusha]]''.<ref group="‡" name="KageStoryteller" />

Conway is regularly invited to tell his stories at other fan conventions, including [[I-CON]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.iconsf.org/archive/icon22/anthro.htm|title=I-CON 22 – Anthropomorphics|access-date=August 27, 2006|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060829012710/http://www.iconsf.org/archive/icon22/anthro.htm|archive-date=August 29, 2006}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.iconsf.org/archive/icon24/anthro_conway.php|title=I-CON 24 Guests – Dr. Samuel Conway|author=ICON Science Fiction|access-date=August 26, 2006|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061004002044/http://iconsf.org/archive/icon24/anthro_conway.php|archive-date=October 4, 2006}}</ref> [[Eurofurence]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.eurofurence.org/EF8/home.html|title=Eurofurence 8|date=June 22, 2002|access-date=August 27, 2006}}</ref><ref group="‡">{{cite web|url=http://www.unclekage.com/ef8/index.html|title=Uncle Kage – How was Eurofurence 8?|author=Conway, Samuel C.|access-date=August 27, 2006}}</ref> ConClave,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.scifiinc.net/scifiinc/gallery/list/cons/duckon.htm|title=Duckon Reference for Fan Gallery|access-date=August 27, 2006|archive-date=September 27, 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070927030137/http://www.scifiinc.net/scifiinc/gallery/list/cons/duckon.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref> and Camp Feral!. Gross sales from recordings of his ''Story Hours'' were over US$2600 in 2004; no profit was realized, as the intention was to increase membership and awareness of Anthrocon.<ref group="‡">{{cite journal|title=Anthrocon, Inc. – IRS Form 990 – Return of Organization Exempt From Income Tax|date=May 15, 2004|author=Conway, Samuel C.|journal=[[ProPublica]]}}</ref><ref group="‡">{{cite web|url=http://www.unclekage.com/videos.html|title=Uncle Kage's videos|author=Conway, Samuel C.|access-date=August 28, 2007}}</ref>

=== Auctioneer ===
[[Image:LastBrickOfAdamsMarkAtAuctionAnthrocon2006.jpg|right|thumb|200px|In 2006, Conway auctioned the "last brick" of Anthrocon's old venue (the Adam's Mark Hotel) for US$200.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.anthrocon.org/history-charity-2006|title=Anthrocon 2006 Charity Report|access-date=August 27, 2006|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060830143422/http://www.anthrocon.org/history-charity-2006|archive-date=August 30, 2006}}</ref>]]

Conway's first auction was at Albany Anthrocon 1997.<ref group="‡">{{cite web|url=http://www.unclekage.com/auction.html|title=Uncle Kage: The Auctioneer|author=Conway, Samuel C.|access-date=August 27, 2006}}</ref> Since then, he has presided over auctions which have raised over US$66,000 for a variety of local wildlife charities at Anthrocon alone.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.anthrocon.org/charity|title=Anthrocon Charity Auction FAQ|version=9.0|access-date=August 27, 2006}}</ref> He has performed similar services at other fan conventions, including [[Midwest FurFest]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.breuckman.com/pipermail/mff-announce/2008-September/000025.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110708092529/http://www.breuckman.com/pipermail/mff-announce/2008-September/000025.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 8, 2011|title=Midwest FurFest Announces Charity for 2008!|author=Brady, Tom|date=September 15, 2008|access-date=April 3, 2009|author-link=WikiFur:Tom Brady}}</ref> Conway says his techniques are influenced by [[Phil Foglio]] and Joe Mayhew; they include humor and [[appeal to pity|appeals to pity]], [[appeal to novelty|novelty]] and [[scarcity]].<ref name="Pleasures" />

=== Author ===

While known within the fandom for his spoken storytelling, Conway is also the author of several [[short story|short stories]] published in various works by Sofawolf Press.<ref name="KageStoryteller" group="‡"/>

In May 1998, Conway was invited to write a story based on his interest in [[bird of prey|birds of prey]], particularly the [[red-tailed hawk]].<ref name="KageStoryteller" group="‡"/> The result was "Tweaked in the Head", published December 1999 in ''[[Flights of Fantasy]]''.<ref>{{cite book|url=https://archive.org/details/flightsoffantasy00|title=Flights of Fantasy|editor=Lackey, Mercedes|editor2=Greenberg, Martin H.|publisher=[[Daw Book Collectors]]|date=December 1, 1999|isbn=0-88677-863-8|url-access=registration}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sfsite.com/03a/ff76.htm|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20000411165851/http://www.sfsite.com/03a/ff76.htm|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 11, 2000|title=The S.F. Site: ''Flights of Fantasy'', a review.|author=Dobbs, George T.|year=2000|access-date=August 27, 2006}}</ref> He next contributed to the first issue of ''HistoriMorphs'', a [[fanzine]] mixing [[historical fiction]] with interaction between humans and anthropomorphic animals.<ref name="KageStoryteller" group="‡"/> "The Secret of Wollknäul" took place in [[Nazi Germany]] at the end of [[World War II]], and was published in June 2001.<ref>{{cite book|url=http://www.rabbitvalley.com/item_1356_2419___Historimorphs-Issue-Number-1.html|title=HistoriMorphs I|editor=Fields, Lanny|publisher=Sofawolf Press|date=July 1, 2001|access-date=August 27, 2006}}</ref> He went on to write "The Good Bird of Nanking" and "It Takes A Fox" for subsequent issues of the series.<ref>{{cite book|url=http://www.sofawolf.com/catalog/product_info.php?products_id=43|title=HistoriMorphs II|publisher=Sofawolf Press|date=June 25, 2004|access-date=August 27, 2006|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070513113507/http://www.sofawolf.com/catalog/product_info.php?products_id=43|archive-date=May 13, 2007}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|url=http://www.sofawolf.com/catalog/product_info.php?products_id=60|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070104032841/http://www.sofawolf.com/catalog/product_info.php?products_id=60|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 4, 2007|title=HistoriMorphs III|publisher=Sofawolf Press|date=May 31, 2006|access-date=August 27, 2006}}</ref>

For ''Anthrolations #5''—a magazine of dramatic fiction—Conway submitted "Six", a previously-written work "based on a true story" involving [[wildlife rehabilitation]] from his days as a Red Cross volunteer.<ref name="KageStoryteller" group="‡"/><ref>{{cite book|url=http://www.sofawolf-press.de/en/products.html|title=Our Products|publisher=Sofawolf Press|date=July 27, 2002|access-date=August 27, 2006}}</ref> The story, illustrated by ''Synnabar'', was nominated for "Best Anthropomorphic Short Story" in the 2002 Ursa Major Awards.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ursamajorawards.org/UMA_2002.htm|title=The Ursa Major Awards – 2002 winners|date=April 25, 2003|access-date=August 28, 2006}}</ref> Also nominated that year was ''Breaking the Ice: Stories from New Tibet'', a collection set in and around a subarctic mining colony; Conway's contribution, "Dead End", features a bartending vulture who provides an introduction to the harsh, dystopic world.<ref>{{cite book|url=http://www.sofawolf.com/catalog/product_info.php?products_id=44|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050218221753/http://www.sofawolf.com/catalog/product_info.php?products_id=44|url-status=dead|archive-date=February 18, 2005|title=Breaking the Ice (Stories from New Tibet)|editor=Susman, Tim|date=January 1, 2002|publisher=Sofawolf Press|access-date=August 27, 2006|isbn=0-9712670-0-6}}</ref>

=== Charity work ===
In 2012, Conway learned that Fernando's, a local restaurant, was going to be closing down due to financial trouble. Fernando's had welcomed Anthrocon guests and furries since Anthrocon moved to Pittsburgh. After putting word out on Twitter and YouTube, over $21,000 was raised in donations to keep the restaurant in business.<ref group="‡">{{cite web|url=http://unclekage.livejournal.com/140100.html|title=Helping Fernando |author=Conway, Samuel C.|date=April 15, 2012|access-date=November 5, 2013}}</ref>

== Other activities ==

While in college, Conway was a member of the Ursinius [[Meistersinger]]s vocal music group, and the performing arts honor society [[Pi Nu Epsilon]].<ref name="LinkedIn" /> He became a volunteer for the [[American Red Cross]] Disaster Service in 1989, but quit in 1998 due to his perception of high-level [[Political corruption|corruption]] in the organization. He was an [[Emergency management|Emergency Management Coordinator]] while residing in [[Malvern, Pennsylvania]].<ref name="NewJob" group="‡" /><ref name="KageTheMan" group="‡"/><ref name="LinkedIn" />

In March 1990, Conway became an experimental [[bone marrow]] donor for Mark Stevenson, a 4-year-old with [[Hunter syndrome]].<ref name="Oskaloosa" >{{cite news|title=Leighton boy celebrates 5 years after|author=Hardesty, Tom|publisher=[[The Oskaloosa Herald]], Vol. 145, No. 163|date=March 14, 1995}}</ref><ref group="‡">{{cite web|title=PSA: Save a life while you sleep!|url=http://unclekage.livejournal.com/6735.html|author=Conway, Samuel C.|date=September 21, 2004|access-date=April 11, 2009}}</ref><!--Blog provided since the Oskaloosa story, which also contains all referenced facts, is not online.--> The operation was the first of its kind involving an unrelated donor, and was successful; Mark lived to 24.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://obituaries.pellachronicle.com/obituary/mark-stevenson-1986-771232891|title=Obituary: Mark Stevenson|publisher=Pella Chronicle|date=March 29, 2010}}</ref> Conway became an active volunteer for the [[National Marrow Donor Program]], claiming to have helped add over 500 entries to their donor registry.<ref name="Oskaloosa" />

Since May 1996, Conway has participated in the [[MadSci Network]], a free question-and-answer Ask-A-Scientist forum organized by the [[Washington University School of Medicine|medical school]] of [[Washington University in St. Louis]].<ref name="KageTheMan" group="‡"/><ref name="MadSci" /><ref group="‡">{{cite web|url=http://www.madsci.org/posts/archives/1996-05/826296888.Ch.r.html|title=Re: Properties of Solutions|author=Conway, Samuel C.|publisher=MadSci Network|date=May 13, 1996|access-date=April 3, 2009}}</ref> While most active in the period 1997–2000,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.madsci.org/cgi-bin/search?query=Samuel+Conway|title=MadSci Search Results for Samuel Conway|access-date=August 27, 2006}}</ref> he remains a member as of 2009.<ref group="‡">{{cite web|title=Re: Lifespan of HIV in contact with air?|url=http://www.madsci.org/posts/archives/2008-03/1204991105.Vi.r.html|author=Conway, Samuel C.|publisher=MadSci Network|date=March 6, 2008|access-date=April 3, 2009}}</ref><ref group="‡">{{cite web|title=Re: Would inhaling ethanol based gasoline fumes effect a breathalyzer|url=http://www.madsci.org/posts/archives/2009-02/1234393471.Ch.r.html|author=Conway, Samuel C.|publisher=MadSci Network|date=February 11, 2009|access-date=April 3, 2009}}</ref>
